text: A) EMERGENCY - life or limb in immediate danger (for example breathing trouble, collapse or unresponsiveness, seizure, severe bleeding, poisoning, stroke or heart-attack signs, serious danger in pregnancy or to a newborn, suicidal intent). Staff must be alerted right now.
B) URGENT - needs a doctor the same day but is not immediately life-threatening.
C) ROUTINE - can wait for a normal appointment (mild or long-standing problems, check-ups, reports, refills).
D) INSUFFICIENT - too vague to judge; more questions are needed.
If torn between two levels, choose the more urgent one.
